items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: And Woody had a good band.

ctx.x: Now, when you had a repertoire this size, how did the guys -- did they memorize most of that music?

Two-thirds. Two thirds of it was memorized. Duke insisted on that. Because it mystified the average band, He wouldn't have to call 23 or 44 or different numbers, because when we started playing we would pay eight or 16 bars, just him and I and the bass. Anything. But when it got down near the last six bars, he would give them a tonic so the boys in the band would know what number we're playing. And he would turn around and give them that direct cue. So he would look at me and I would say to the guys, "we're…

That's how we -- and they never could understand. None of the bands'dn understand know what we were doing. Count does a little of it, you know. I noticed at the concert he would play not every number, but he would play a little--you know how Count Basie--tinkle it a little bit. And get up there and do like this and the band would shout. Well, he got that from Duke. Ain't no "one-two, one-two" you know, like Lawrence Welk or Woody Herman, all them bands.
